segments.text: This level is a lesson about git history: the current README has the password replaced with a row of x characters.
I log in as bandit28 with ssh bandit28@bandit.labs.overthewire.org -p 2220.
The lab blocks the localhost ssh hop, so I clone from this client.
Git pulls nine objects and checks out the working tree.
I open the README, and the password is redacted to x's.
But git keeps every previous version: the log shows three commits, and the latest is titled fix info leak.
The parent of the redaction still holds the real password, so I ask git to show that older version of the README.
There it is: the password for bandit twenty-nine, and the level is solved.
